subject: Tryout extension: invoice vs credit options
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena@novacare.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: Novacare Procurement <procurement@novacare.ai>
Date: 2026-11-18T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Tryout: extension request and billing options

Hi Jasmine,

We are approaching the end of our 30-day tryout (scheduled to conclude on 2026-11-30) and the team would like to extend for another 3 weeks to finish a final integration test and a compliance review. Before we loop procurement in formally, can you outline the options you can offer for: a) a short time-box extension invoiced pro-rata, b) a credit bucket we can draw from, or c) a complimentary or courtesy extension tied to conversion timing?

Also, procurement needs to know if an extension that increases concurrency will require any capacity reservation or an amended SOW. Attaching a short requirements summary.

Appreciate a quick rundown — we are aiming to finalize by next Thursday so procurement can process payment if needed.

Thanks,
Elena Torres
Head of AI Integrations
Novacare

Attachment: Novacare_requirements.pdf (1 page summary)
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <elena@novacare.ai>
Cc: Novacare Procurement <procurement@novacare.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-18T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Tryout: extension request and billing options

Elena —

Thanks for the note and for the requirements doc. We have three pragmatic paths we typically offer for short tryout extensions:

• Pro-rated invoice: we can issue a one-off invoice for the extra days (prorated by daily token estimate). This is straightforward for procurement and keeps billing clean on their side.
• Credit bucket: issue X tokens as a credit you can draw down; useful if usage timing is uncertain and you prefer to avoid another invoice. Credits are valid for 90 days.
• Courtesy extension tied to conversion: we can grant a one-time complimentary 14-day extension if you sign a conversion or reserved capacity commitment by a set date.

A couple of tradeoffs to call out: if you expect sustained higher concurrency during the extension we may need to reserve capacity (small fee) to guarantee latency. If not, we can run the extra load on hosted capacity subject to transient throttling.

If procurement prefers invoicing, let us know whether they require a PO before we issue. If you want, I can propose specific numbers (days -> token estimate -> pro-rate) after a quick usage sanity check.

Options I recommend for Novacare based on current telemetry: either a 3-week pro-rated invoice (least operational friction) or the 14-day courtesy + conversion discount (if you plan to commit). Which direction should I prep language for?

—Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>, Elena Torres <elena@novacare.ai>
Date: 2026-11-18T14:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Tryout: extension request and billing options

On Wed, Nov 18, 2026 at 11:03 AM Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Elena —
> 
> Thanks for the note and for the requirements doc. We have three pragmatic paths we typically offer for short tryout extensions:
> 
> • Pro-rated invoice...

Quick technical note from my side — thanks for the usage summary, Elena. A few operational items to be explicit about:

• If Novacare will spike to >120 concurrent requests for sustained periods during the extension, we should reserve a small dedicated lane (this ensures KV cache warmness and consistent P95 latency). That reservation is a fixed daily fee and can be billed pro-rata.
• If you remain below that threshold, we can continue on shared hosted capacity with no reservation fee; worst case you might see slightly higher tail latency during peak minutes.
• No code changes are required either way; just a routing/reservation toggle on our side.

I've attached a short CSV with the capacity option breakouts (daily reservation fee vs shared). If you want me to model the pro-rated invoice numbers I can do that quickly with your average daily token usage.

—David
David Kim
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachment: capacity_options.csv (stub)
From: Elena Torres <elena@novacare.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Novacare Procurement <procurement@novacare.ai>
Date: 2026-11-19T09:46:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Tryout: extension request and billing options

Thanks David and Jasmine — helpful. A few clarifying items from procurement:

1) Procurement prefers an invoice (not credit) for auditing reasons. They will accept a short-term invoice if we attach a statement of work or amendment indicating dates and scope.
2) PO process: they can issue a PO if the amount is under $25k; anything above that needs expedited legal review.
3) SOC2/audit: they asked whether the extension invoice needs any special line items referencing data residency — not necessary for us but they want it documented.

Can Redwood produce a 21-day pro-rated invoice (2026-12-01 to 2026-12-21) and an SOW amendment that states "trial extension and capacity reservation (if elected)"? If you can draft the SOW text we can route it through procurement.

I attached a one-page requirements overview — happy to jump on a 20-minute call if helpful.

Elena

Attachment: Novacare_requirements.pdf (resubmitted)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <elena@novacare.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-20T15:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Tryout: extension request and billing options

Elena —

Appreciate the clear ask and timeline. To help Novacare move quickly, Redwood will do the following one-time concession:

• Issue a pro-rated invoice for 21 days (2026-12-01 to 2026-12-21) based on your current daily token consumption estimate.
• Provide a short SOW amendment for the extension language and an explicit line for "capacity reservation" that can be toggled on if you elect the reservation.
• Additionally, if Novacare signs a 6-month reserved capacity commitment by 2026-12-15, we'll apply a 15% credit against the first monthly invoice.

Next steps I will take today: draft the invoice numbers and a one-page SOW amendment and send both to procurement + DocuSign link. Jasmine, please confirm the daily token estimate you want used for the pro-rate and whether procurement requires the PO field filled before we issue the invoice.

Marissa Cole
Director, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
